title: Proper direct-image scalar comparison for all-continuous algebraic closure coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. Put $A_E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets with its norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $A_{E,T}=p_T^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects, ordinary unbounded derived module categories and their derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Constructible means finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Put $B(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ using ALL continuous maps, $B_T=p_T^*B$, and let $A_{E,T}\to B_T$ be induced by the continuous inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Write $T_T=B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. For a morphism $f:Z\to T$, define $\beta_{f,K}:T_TRf_{*,A_E}K\to Rf_{*,B}T_ZK$ to be the adjunct under $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ of $f_B^*T_TRf_{*,A_E}K\cong T_Zf_{A_E}^*Rf_{*,A_E}K\xrightarrow{T_Z\varepsilon}T_ZK$, with canonical pullback/tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No completion or filtered-union coefficient interpretation is made.

For every proper $k$-morphism $f:Z\to T$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and every $K\in\Dbc(Z,A_E)$, the specified canonical morphism $\beta_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism. This assertion does not require that $T_ZK$ or either resulting direct image be constructible, and does not assume flatness of the condensed coefficient map.

proof.text: Distinguish the two algebraic-closure coefficient rings: let $C$ be the finite-subextension-valued ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and retain $B$ from the item. The inclusions give $A_E\xrightarrow a C\xrightarrow c B$. Write $S_W=C_W\otimes^L_{A_{E,W}}-$ and $J_W=B_W\otimes^L_{C_W}-$. The canonical balanced associator identifies $J_WS_W$ with $T_W$. All three rings are pulled back from the point, so [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies their geometric inverse images with their source coefficients. Work through the exact monoidal internal/section-module equivalence [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison]. Then the associators and the normalized scalar push comparisons are those of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]; they apply to $a,c$ without a flatness hypothesis. Denote the three counit-mate push comparisons by $\chi_a,\chi_c,\chi_{ca}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3): coefficient rings and canonical maps, agent expansion

proof.text: Put $L=S_ZK$. It is bounded constructible by [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible]. Since $f$ is proper between the standing schemes, clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational], used with coefficient $C$, gives $P=Rf_{*,C}L\in D^b_c(T,C)$. Clause (1) of the same node, applied to the bounded-below $A_E$-complex $K$, says that the canonical map $\chi_{a,K}:S_TRf_{*,A_E}K\to Rf_{*,C}L$ is invertible. This invocation is solely about $C$, not $B$.

Apply [lem-sfb-constructible-algcl-topology-comparison] at $Z$ and $T$. Thus $J_ZL$ and $J_TP$ are bounded constructible. The schemes are Noetherian because they are finite type over a field [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and itself. Hence [det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-constructible-tor] gives finite Tor amplitude for $J_ZL$. The bounded-constructible finite-Tor preservation assertion of [det-sf-comp-proper-continuous-algcl], for the actual all-continuous $B$ and the given proper $f$, gives $Q=Rf_{*,B}J_ZL\in D^b_c(T,B)$. This verifies membership of both endpoints of $\chi_{c,L}:J_TP\to Q$ in the full constructible subcategory.

source.place: Paragraph (3): verify the domains for constructible coefficient comparison

proof.text:
For $M\in D^b_c(T,C)$, pullback preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves]. Write $\sigma_M:f_B^*J_TM\xrightarrow{\sim}J_Zf_C^*M$ for the canonical tensor comparison, normalized by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. The adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and full faithfulness of $J_T,J_Z$ in [lem-sfb-constructible-algcl-topology-comparison] give bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(J_TM,J_TP)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(M,P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(f_C^*M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(J_Zf_C^*M,J_ZL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(J_TM,Q).$$
This composite is precisely postcomposition with $\chi_{c,L}$. Indeed the first bijection writes an arrow as $J_Tu$. Its image under the middle two bijections is $J_Z(\varepsilon_L\circ f_C^*u)$. After precomposition with $\sigma_M$ it is $J_Z\varepsilon_L\circ\sigma_P\circ f_B^*J_Tu$, by naturality of $\sigma$. The adjunct of $J_Z\varepsilon_L\circ\sigma_P$ is the specified $\chi_{c,L}$, so naturality of adjunction gives $\chi_{c,L}\circ J_Tu$. This checks the actual counit mate, rather than a freely chosen isomorphism of its endpoints.

source.place: Paragraph (3): explicit Hom calculation identifying the canonical comparison

proof.text: Essential surjectivity of $J_T$ from [lem-sfb-constructible-algcl-topology-comparison] and step 4 imply that postcomposition with $\chi_{c,L}$ is bijective on $\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,-)$ for every bounded constructible $N$. Both endpoints are in that class by step 3. Taking $N=Q$, surjectivity supplies $v:Q\to J_TP$ with $\chi_{c,L}v=1_Q$. Taking $N=J_TP$, injectivity and $\chi_{c,L}(v\chi_{c,L})=\chi_{c,L}1_{J_TP}$ give $v\chi_{c,L}=1_{J_TP}$. Thus $\chi_{c,L}$ is invertible in the ambient category, whose constructible subcategory is full.

source.place: Paragraph (3): explicit inverse from full faithfulness and essential surjectivity

proof.text:
The coefficient cocycle of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] gives
$$\chi_{ca,K}\circ\tau_T=Rf_{*,B}(\tau_Z)\circ\chi_{c,S_ZK}\circ J_T(\chi_{a,K}),$$
where $\tau_W:J_WS_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W$ is the balanced associator, evaluated at the required complex. Step 2 proves invertibility of $\chi_{a,K}$ and steps 3--5 prove invertibility of $\chi_{c,S_ZK}$. Functors preserve inverses, so every factor on the right, and $\tau_T$, is invertible. Thus $\chi_{ca,K}$ is invertible. Its coefficient map is exactly the original $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ map, and its adjunct is exactly the pullback/tensor comparison followed by $T_Z\varepsilon$ in the item, by the cocycle's definition of $\chi_{ca}$ and step 1's normalization. Therefore $\chi_{ca,K}=\beta_{f,K}$.
